text:
Allergies:
Zidovudine

Chief Complaint:
dyspnea, cough

History of Present Illness:
___ yo F with HIV (last CD4 ___ not on HAART, HCV, afib, 
antiphospholipid ab syndrome, multiple VTEs, CM with EF 20%, 
presents with fever, shortness of breath, cough, headache. She 
complains of fevers, fatigue and productive cough with 
green/yellow sputum. She complains of headache on the right side 
for several days. Denies neck stiffness, chest pain, shortness 
of breath or abdominal pain. No nausea or vomiting. Pt denies 
diarrhea or melena.  She denies sick contacts, no recent 
incarcerations.  Has lived in homeless shelter in the distant 
past, not recently.
.
In the ED, initial vital signs were T 101.6, BP 86/57, HR 108, 
O2sat 96% RA. Her lactate was 1.0. She was given 8L IVF in the 
ED for low blood pressures in the 80-90's systolic. HR was 
80-90s. RSCVL was placed. She was also started on levophed for 
hypotension. Per report, she was mentating normally the entire 
time.  She was given vancomycin for pneumonia on CXR.  She was 
also given levafloxacin, ceftriaxone and bactrim and 60mg 
prednisone for possible PCP. Urine hCG was negative. Urine 
positive for trichomonas.
.
Currently, she continues to complain of cough and shortness of 
breath.  No headache currently.  No abdominal pain, N/V.

Brief Hospital Course:
MICU Course:
.
The patient was admitted to the MICU with possible pneumonia and 
possible sepsis after recieving 8L IV fluids in the ED and a 
lactate of 1.0.  She was quickly weaned off Levophed upon 
arrival to the ICU.  She was initially treated with 
broad-spectrum antibiotics with Vancomycin, Ceftriaxone and 
Levofloxacin.  The vancomycin was stopped on ___ due to low 
suspicion for gram positive pneumonia.  She was started on 
Bactrim DS 2 tabs q8 hours for possible PCP.  Her CD4 count was 
rechecked and was 184.  She was given Prednisone 60mg PO in the 
ED but steroids were not continued because her O2 sats were high 
on minimal oxygen and LDH was normal and this was not felt to be 
severe PCP.  She was ordered for induced sputum for PCP and 
nasal aspirate to check for rapid viral antigens.  She was 
continued on fluconazole for oral thrush and nystatin oral rinse 
was added.
.
Her metoprolol and lisinopril were stopped due to hypotension.  
She had a repeat echo to assess her CHF, which showed LV cavity 
more dilated from ___ with similar systolic function.  The 
severity of MR and the PASP were higher.  She was not felt to be 
in heart failure on arrival to the ICU.  She was put on a 
low-salt diet.  
.
Floor Course:
.
Pt. was transferred to floor on ___ and she continued to 
complain of occasional cough and shortness of breath.  She 
denied other Sx. Her Vitals were 96.2F, 102.68, 96, 18, 99% RA. 
. 
# Fevers/cough/dyspnea.  These were felt to be ___ to multifocal 
CAP, or PCP and patient was continued on Ceftriaxone, 
Levofloxacin and Bactrim DS TID.  She underwent a CT of chest 
which showed extensive rapidly progressive pneumonia in both 
lungs, small bilateral pleural effusions, improving extensive 
chronic lymphadenopathy.  She was intremittently treated with 
Vancomycin IV x 1d for GPC in BCx from ___ w/ GPC that turned 
out to be coag negative staph, vancomycin was thus discontinued. 
 Her Legionella Ag was negative and her Levofloxacin was thus 
discontinued on ___. Cryptococcal Ag was negative as were 
respiratory viral rapid screens.  Patient improved clinically 
significantly, w/ O2 saturations on RA 94-97% and ambulation of 
> ___ yards w/o DOE.  Her induced sputums were repeatedly of poor 
quiality and could not be assessed for PCP ___.  A 
bronchoscopy was considered, however in consultation with ID and 
Pulmonary team it was decided against it due to patient's 
clinical improvement and hypotension (see below).  Her repeat CT 
chest on ___ showed much improved infiltrates b/l consistent 
w/ clinical improvement.  Her dyspnea, cough and fatigue 
continued to improve.  She was afebrile throughout the hosptial 
stay w/ good perfusion on exam.  Due to progressive leukopenia, 
ANC 580, her Bactrim was switched to Atovaquone (total 21-day 
course of 750mg PO bid, day 4 on day of discharge, then 1500mg 
qday for prophylaxis) with subsequent return of WBC count to 2.5 
and ANC to 1180. 
On ___, her Ceftriaxone IV was switched to Cefpodoxime 200mg 
PO BID.  She should complete the course of total of 14days of 
Ceftriaxone/Cefpodoxime.  Repeat induced sputum smear/Cx ___ 
showed oropharygeal flora. PCP smear was pending.  Beta glucan 
was pending at time of discharge. Pt will require CT within 2 
weeks and ID f/u within ___ re-check of 
ANC.
.
Patient's previously "positive" TST were documented as negative 
upon chart review with ID.  She was treated for ___ in the past, 
but this was felt to be a colonizer.  Please see note from ID 
staff on ___ for more detail.
.  
# Hypotension.  Patient was triggered for hypotension, SBPs 
___ on ___ and ___.  She was asymptomatic during this 
time (no dizziness, lightheadedness, chest pain, shortness of 
breath, changes in MS). Her baseline from ___ OP visit was SBP 
of 90mmHg.  She responded to 500cc bolus and maitenance fluids 
to 90mmHg.  Patient was signficantly volume negative on I/Os, 
felt to be secondary to post ATN diuresis. She was ruled out for 
adrenal insufficiency w/ a negative cortosyn stimulation test.  
Poor contractility given CHF w/ EF 20% and falling off 
Frank-starling curve were considered, but patient was perfusing 
well and was asymptomatic througout this time.  She was also 
started on low dose digoxin, 62.5mcg to improve forward flow.  K 
was closely monitored and remained wnl throughout hospital stay. 
 Upon maintaining fluid balance over next 3 HDs w/ IVF boluses 
and maintenance fluids, her SBPs returned to 80-100mmHg.  Her 
Metoprolol and Lisinopril were held throughout this time.  These 
were restarted at metoprolol XL 12.5 and Lisinopril 2.5. He was 
continued on 0.0625 mg of digoxin to aid w/ contractility. 
Culture data as mentioned above were pending at time of 
discharge. 
.  
# Leukopenia. Patient developed leukopenia 3.8-->1.9->2.1-> 
2.5-> 2.9, ANC 1170. Improved after D/ced bactrim (___). WBC 
from her previous hospitalizations ranged 2.5-4K.  This was felt 
to be likely ___ Bactrim, or HIV itself.  There were no clinical 
signs of MAC, Histoplasma, EBV, hepatitis (which pt has), CMV. 
Her retic count was hypoproliferative.  Fe studies were 
consistent w/ ACD.  Folate/B12 were wnl.  ANC troughed at 580, 
and improved to 1170 on day of discharge.
.  
# ARF. Cr elevated to 1.4 on admission, likely ___ sepsis.  It 
improved temporarily and then increased to 1.4 within 5d of 
admission with increased U/O consistent with post ATN duiresis. 
FeNa was > 6%.  U/A showed no evidence of a glomerular process 
nor casts.  Efforts were made to keep patient I/Os even.  At 
time of discharge, her Cr. improved to 0.9 and her U/O 
stabilized.
.  
#  Chronic pulmonary micronodulation on CT.  Previously 
attributed to non tuberculous mycobacterial infection.  This 
actually improved on CT scans while hospitalized.  LAD had also 
decreased on repeat scans.  Etiology of these is unclear and 
outpatient follow up was recommeneded.  
.  
# Cardiomyopathy.  Pt. was euvolemic on exam. Has chronic, 
systolic, HIV related vs. cocaine related, non-ischemic CHF: EF 
___.  Echo this admission with increased LV dilatation and 
increased PA pressures. This was likely ___ IVF and increase 
pulmonary resistance ___ PNA.  Pt. had new inversion of Tw in 
inferior leads and old lateral lead inversions. CE were negative 
x2.  No events noted on telemetry suggestive of ischemia.  ACEI 
was initially held ___ to hypotension as was BBK.  This as well 
as metoprolol and digoxin were resumed as BP improved, and 
continued at time of discharge. Patient was maintained on low Na 
diet.
.
# Substance Abuse.  Pt denied cocaine on this interview but had 
a positive tox screen.  Social work consult was obtained. She 
endorsed illusions to ___ staff, but denied these to medical 
staff.  She was not interested in discussing this topic further. 
  
.  
# Afib Hx in chart, but could not locate documentation in OMR.  
Patient was in sinus rhythm throughout hospitalization.    
.  
# Antiphospholipid syndrome. Multiple VTEs.  Patient's coumadin 
was held ___ supratherapeutic INRs, likely ___ 
fluconazole and levofloxacin.  Her coumadin was restarted at 5mg 
QD and titrated to target INR of ___. She was strongly advised 
not to ___ upcoming ___ appointment for INR re-check.
.  
# HIV/AIDS. CD4 count 184. VL 254K. Patient will likely require 
HAART, but previously not on therapy due to poor compliance. 
Already on fluconazole for PPx. No need for CMV ppx as CD4 > 50. 
Discussed with ID, patient will likely start HAART as outpatient 
once adherence to appts can be documented.  Continued atovaquone 
and fluconazole.  
.  
# Depression w/ hx of anxeity sx. per patient, fluoxetine was 
not helping and she was not currently taking it. Continue 
ativan. Pt. is willing to try celexa as outpatient.
.  
# Difficulties adhering to care. Contributed to by difficult 
home situation (one daughter jailed) and the other daughter 
reportedly not supportive at home. In addition, patient 
reporting difficulties getting to her appointments.  After 
discussion with social work and case managment, pt was set up 
with transportation assistance.
.
Patient was discharged home in a hemodynamically stable 
condition with multiple ___ appointments.

Discharge Diagnosis:
Primary: Pneumonia, Sepsis
Secondary: Heart failure, HIV/AIDS, coronary artery disease, 
multiple pulmonary emboli
